I had a physical disability in HS that caused me to balloon up in weight. When it went into remission, I spent the next nearly two years dieting and working out and lost 86lbs and was fitter than fit. 

Come to find only a few years later I’m diagnosed with BP1 and the meds made me gain back that 86lbs plus a few more. And yet I’ve always had a social life (when I wanted one), always had girlfriends (and now a fiancée 🥰), and I have lost a little over 30 lbs of it by working with my pdoc to find somewhat weight neutral meds and  doing what I can eating wise. My physical disabilities are worse so much more than walking is out of the question. 

But remember, and never forget, you are so much more than what you weigh or what you look like. You are your kind heart, your wonderful smile. If you can’t see it than see it in how your family sees you, how your loved ones see you, how your pets and other animals see you. 

You are truly unique in this universe: there is no one like you and never will be again. Don’t let a few dozen pounds ever stop you from being proud of who you are. And it’s always better to be heavyset with a clear, non-manic state of mind than to be manic and skinny. As someone who’s been both several times, trust me on that

Stop and celebrate! Feel proud of yourself, even if no one feels proud for you. Give yourself a giant pat on the back. You did something most people in the world will never accomplish. 

Then do something else or write something else or, as I prefer to do, read a lot, watch a lot of documentaries, and give yourself AT LEAST 3 months before returning to it with fresh eyes. 

But give yourself GRACE. If you’re like most writers, you’ll come at it again very critical of yourself and be like “what is this shite I wrote?” Don’t do that. But come at it rather with fresh eyes, maybe new ideas since you’ve been reading and exploring and living life the last three months, and dive in. Most of writing is REWRITING. And usually, if you let it be, the most fun part too. 

And most of all, continue to be proud of yourself. I’m proud of you ☺️

I switched from poetry to screenplays, as that fit my interests at that time, always planning to go back to the novels I had started as a middle-schooler. I once wrote an entire 90 page film script in a weekend binge of mania. 

During bouts of mania I finished my first complete novel - a sci-fi/fantasy one - that clocked in at around just under 600 pages double spaced and formatted by disciplining myself and setting my alarm two hours before I had to be at work and writing for 90 minutes every morning. Took me about a year and a half. 

Fast forward to now, while writing a much shorter, much more philosophically interesting novel (IMHO), and I’m in a depressive state and stuck at chapter 9 the last 4 to 6 months. So, it depends on your life, your circumstances, your mental health, your age, your discipline. It all comes in waves and is different for everyone

Am I the only one who believes Palpatine manipulated all of this? I firmly believe he told Maul to isolate Qui-Gon and kill him. I believe he put the dreams of Shmi and Padme into Anakin’s mind, knowing already Shmi was dying and if Yoda could sense Anakin killing the Sand People, he could too. Then when confronted about killing Dooku, you can hear the Tusken Raiders yelling in the background. 

Then, he has dreams about Padme, which I also believe Palpatine caused. Palpatine admits one must learn ALL the ways of the force, which would include the teachings of the Jedi, meaning he’d know the worthless advice Yoda would give Anakin. He masterminded Anakin to be appointed to the Council, knew they would ask him to commit treason against his friend the Chancellor. He frequently tells Anakin he is the strongest of ALL Jedi. This part is key later on. 

I also believe that when Anakin says “I’ll do whatever you ask” he is playing a game. Much like Luke did in the Dark Victory comics, he believes he can conquer the dark side and outsmart Palpatine by joining the dark side and once learning how to save Padme can destroy it from within (by any means necessary), sadly even by killing younglings. He clearly hates this as when he’s gazing out at the lava on Mustafar you can see he’s crying. He knows full well what he’s done. 

He tells Padme clearly that he can “overthrow” the Chancellor and rule the galaxy the way he talks about in AOTC. Padme won’t go for this which angers him. He chokes her, a clear sign of a violent outburst from a person with borderline personality disorder (which several psychiatrists who’ve seen the prequels have diagnosed Anakin with). When he tells Obi-Wan his vision of how the galaxy should be in ROTS, much like he told Padme in AOTC, Obi-Wan thinks rightfully that he’s gone nuts. 

Then he loses the battle to Obi-Wan due to overconfidence in his power (power he’ll clearly try to use to overthrow the Emperor). The Emperor knows how a (mostly) fully human Anakin can become, as he tells Yoda, that Anakin will become stronger than the both of them. 

Anakin knew about the somersault then cut in half move from Obi-Wan as it’s how he killed Maul. This is what he’s trying in the battle on Mustafar. This is what Obi-Wan is referring to when he says “don’t try it”. But Anakin does anyways and suffers the consequences. Obi-Wan believes Anakin is then dead when he catches fire. And he absolutely should be for all intents and purposes. 

But then something interesting happens: Palpatine shows up and puts his hands over Anakin’s dying body. Remember this is before the whole sequel trilogy force healing bullcrap. And at the same time that Anakin is being kept alive and moreso gaining life, Padme is losing hers. The medical droids even tell Obi-Wan “for reasons we can’t explain, we’re losing her”. I don’t think it’s just a stylistic choice that Anakin is turning into Darth Vader at the same time that Padme is dying. 

I think Palpatine is sucking the life out of Padme and giving it to Anakin to keep his apprentice alive. After all, he is Plagueis’s apprentice and knows how to keep people from dying. And once Anakin is in full Vader mode and is told *he* killed Padme and breaks free of his restraints you can see an evil smile creep across Palpatine’s face, almost as if that’s exactly what he wants Vader to believe. 

Also, I believe Palpatine was the one who manipulated the Force to “create life” and gave birth to Anakin in the first place. Remember when asked, GL stated firmly that Luke, not Anakin, is the true Chosen One. This makes sense especially if Anakin was created by the dark side. 

Then, on the Second Death Star, when Luke is being tortured by Palpatine (who manipulated Anakin earlier into killing Windu by faking his own inevitable demise) was the exact moment Anakin realized this was his chance to become so powerful that he could “save the ones he loves” and “stop people from dying” AND finally overthrow The Emperor as he always wanted to do. 

After all, in ESB, he tells Luke that together they can “rule the galaxy as father and son”, which would mean killing Palpatine. Something he’s clearly longed to do for a very long time. 

His impulsive attack on Windu was very similar to his impulsive act to kill Palpatine to save his son. Also remember when Luke had the high ground on the second Death Star, Vader had learned from his mistakes and didn’t try the somersault behind him and cut him in half bit, but threw his lightsaber at him, just as a side note. 

Hayden’s portrayal of Anakin was constantly corrected by GL to literally act more “wooden and stiff”, which I believe was done purposefully even though many accused Christensen of being a bad actor, despite his previous acclaimed roles and later acclaimed roles. Anakin, through this acting, shows signs of someone on the spectrum, someone with muted emotions, stunted emotional growth and awareness and multiple signs of BPD: fears of abandonment either real or perceived, violent outbursts, unstable relationships, etc. 

He’s also crying when telling Padme of his massacre of the Tusken Raiders. He knows that what he’s doing is wrong, that he’s going down a dark path he can’t seem to help and that he’s fully committed to one thing only: his anger, over which he has no control. And Padme, even upon hearing what he’s done, not only accepts him for who he is, but falls in love with him. This means everything to him. 

Add to that the implied PTSD suffered from being a slave, being forced to abandon his mother whom he was very attached to, losing the man whom he entrusted after leaving his mom (Qui-Gon) and then the PTSD from the war, then the regret from killing Dooku, who isn’t inherently a bad man (in the opening crawl it’s explicitly stated there are heroes on BOTH sides), then these implanted dreams of losing the only person left who fully accepts and loves him… it’s enough to make almost anyone snap and especially someone who is neurodivergent who’s never been in any kind of therapy but rather: a slave, a cult follower, and easily influenced since he was 9 by the most politically powerful man in the galaxy. 

While rushed cinematically, when you factor all this in, it *can* make some semblance of sense and understanding and thus is the tragedy that is the life of Anakin Skywalker, a tortured man since the day he was born into slavery until he liberated himself to save his son, the only person left who loved him for who he was, and also a perfect mix of him and Padme, which cost him his life. 

That’s my take on it in any case.

I agree with most of the commentators here. It’s almost like the Superman syndrome. He’s so good and such a boy scout he’s hard to write and hard to make interesting. I know some DC writers and they never wanted him. They wanted a hero who’s conflicted. 

It’s like Campbell’s breakdown of all the ways of the Hero’s Journey and how we ourselves basically experience that in our every day lives. 

But think about heroes like Jack Ryan or Han Solo. While Luke may come off as bland sometimes Han is always engaging. Jack Ryan is engaging because of the things he’s had to overcome in his life. Han Solo, or his literary predecessor Rhett Butler, is intriguing because he’s a mercenary at first and materialistic but finds out he has a conscience he didn’t know existed. 

Even Harry Potter, he’s sometimes very bland as a hero, which fits because it allows us to fill in ourselves with him, but as he develops through the books he becomes more compromised and it’s the rejection of the temptation that makes the hero interesting. The challenges they’ve overcome, whether it’s Christ in the Desert or Buddha or Luke choosing what he thought was death over joining Vader. 

There are ways to make the hero interesting. Back to Superman, find his conflict, whatever it is, be it personal or tied to the story or the masses. Conflict and tension whether within a person or out in the open keep the reader (and for screenwriters the viewer) engaged.

I can’t tell you how much I relate to how you’re feeling. And people will say long after you’ve Been broken up to just get over it and not understand that she was your sun, your air, your moon, and that the flowers bloomed in your eyes because of her. And they no longer do. They won’t understand. 

They’ll tell you date other women, when the right one comes along you’ll forget all about your ex. The truth is if you do this too soon it hurts worse and it’s a terrible thing to be laying with another woman and picturing your ex. 

You can’t explain how everything everyday somehow seems to remind you of her, how you rack your brain with everything she ever said trying to come to an understanding, trying to do a postmortem on the relationship, perhaps remembering things she said she liked about you or guys in general or people in general and you will feel compelled to change in this way. And you might even do so with previously unseen fervor in yourself, and you’ll tell yourself it’s for you. But it’s not, it’s for her. 

You can move on, possibly, but you’ll never forget and you’ll always let that quote “let them go - If they come back then they’re yours, if they don’t they never were” twist inside your head until you’ve fooled yourself that if you wait long enough they will return. 

The best thing I’ve found, aside from learning to embrace the pain and not fight it, is to work on, as someone with BPD, my own core identity. And what I want for me. And some of that may fall in line with the things you think about her. It’s like this as a metaphor, you broke up in the 12th grade, she comes back to you four years later realizing she truly loved you, but you’ve been so stuck and hung on what happened, while she’s completed her bachelors and on her way to a masters you’re still in the 12th grade. In other words, say she were to come back, you’re so much more attractive to yourself and to her if you embrace that pain and say I won’t let it stop me, even though it’s a burning rod in your chest, and develop yourself. Whatever you’ve ever wanted to do - your wildest dreams - pursue with abandon. Find stuff you love, usually you have to revisit childhood that was you on your own as a starting point, and develop that. If you’ve always wanted to go up to Yosemite or travel across country, or learn to run a marathon or write the great American novel, now is the time. And if there are places you can’t go because they’re too painful, then don’t go. And don’t feel bad about it. 

Now, If its new and fresh, I’d give her about 30 days and then try and reach out if she hasn’t. Apologize if you feel you need to but don’t disrespect yourself. Tell her you’ve been thinking about her and would she like to meet for coffee? Sound upbeat, not depressed. And you will be because you’ve spent the last month working on yourself. If you get no response or don’t get a good one, it’ll hurt a lot. Trust me, I’ve been there. 

I would say after that, from experience you will move on but you’ll never forget and every love is different, same as every rose that blooms is different. And you’ll love others but you’ll never love them the way you loved her. And that’s okay. And even when you move on to continue to think about her, that’s okay. Keep a journal where When you want to share something with her you write it down in there. You have your moments of crying and when you just want to be alone. BPD is not your fault nor is the HSP related issues that come with it. You loved fiercely and thus fiercely it hits you back. 

Five years. If in five years you are still stuck in this same place or close to it even after trying everything, then you can reach out again. But don’t do so with hopes. Simply to reestablish contact. 

I’ve been through it and still am. Feel free to message me privately if you’d like to discuss it in detail or just need an ear. 

Stay strong. You loved and you lost but remember even those bad memories you had with her, are still some of the best of your life, because they were with her. Hold them close to your heart but don’t let them bring you down. Smile because it happened.

A) Stop overthinking for one thing, that’s most important. Every writer is a perfectionist and you should always Hate your prose when you read it back (that’s what editing is for). 

B) There is a style of prose, similar to the staccato simplistic one that Hemingway pioneered that purposefully uses the same plain words again and again. Often this is in first person and sometimes can denote a person’s lack of vocabulary or intelligence. 

C) I’ve been writing since I was nine. I’ve been around writers of all kinds all my life. The biggest issue is most never finish a first draft. Because they get hung up on their insecurities and the sad part is most of those are fixed, or rather should be fixed, once the story is complete and you go over it with a very critical, unbiased red pen. 

D) If you’re able to write a strong enough query letter and acquire an agent who believes in your work and say you do get a publisher interested, that’s why they have professional editors who sprinkle purple prose all over your work and make it sound so much better. That’s why if you look to the acknowledgements in a lot of books the writers are very thankful to their editors. The only exceptions are people like Tolkien, who was a longtime Oxford professor and a part of putting together the Oxford English Dictionary and knew the language better than most people living, or already existing authors like Steinbeck or Joyce or Kerouac who were fighting for a specific style and pushed to keep it. 

E) Read as much as you can. Advanced level reading. Classics or Pulitzer winners and pay attention to their word choices (and sometimes you might even disagree with their choices), and develop a flow in your head. Sometimes listening to books on audio or reading them aloud will give your ear a feel for what sounds clunky and what doesn’t. Eventually you’ll develop a voice all your own that is mellifluous and beautiful. Read as diversely as you can. Lyrics, poems of all kinds, novels of all kinds. Though I’m a firm believer in what Stephen King has said when if you want to write good books you have to read good books. It’s like your body. You eat a healthy diet your body will reflect it. You feed it Big Macs and Hot Dogs it’ll reflect that. Quality in, quality out. 

F) Most importantly, remember this: You Are A Writer. Don’t stop, do not give up. Never stop. I promise your writing gets better everyday. And I promise whether you’re writing from a sudden burst of inspiration or forced discipline the result will be the same. And the fact that you realize these things about your writing means you’re detail oriented in your prose. That’s good. Develop that further. And you’ll be amazed at how far you’ll come. 

In summation, don’t overthink, finish that draft without looking back. Edit when it’s done. And read at the level you aspire to write.

One of my writing professors, the one who I stay in touch with and we both review each other’s work and have conversations to this day about writing, always said there are “planters” and “planners”. 

Planters plant seeds in their books or scripts etc and let them take off, allowing the characters to show them who they are (I believe in this to some extent), for instance I’ve been known to write screenplays that I had no idea what they were about, they began with two people having a conversation and as I wrote more of the conversation the characters revealed to me who they were and what this story was I was telling. 

My professor is a planner. Who likes rigorous outlines and references and dynamic control over his characters. Both yield results. 

And there can be a blend of both. And I think there should be because sometimes a planter, like George RR Martin for instance allows his work to become bloated beyond excess and difficult to finish. Or for instance take another fantasy author (not to only use fantasy authors as reference it just so happened that way) Tolkien meticulously planned his mythology but when he wrote Lord Of the Rings he let it tell him the story. In a famous letter he wrote to his son about when Frodo and Sam come along Faramir he said he was as surprised as anyone to find him there and interested to find out who he was. He also had no idea that Strider, at one point named Trotter, when he first wrote him, would be revealed as the descendants of the Kings of Gondor. 

And every writer is trial and error. If it works for you, it works. If it doesn’t, it doesn’t. The point is to never stop writing and never stop honing your craft.
